A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VaLiK, with matching methods, benchmark evaluations and retained appendix content. The text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VaLiK evaluations on CrisisMMD and ScienceQA, component ablations and VLM-count experiments in Tables 1–5 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and adds construction-cost estimates and qualitative findings about pruning and VLM configurations.

M1.justification: The cascaded VLM descriptions, CLIP-based pruning and LightRAG construction with hybrid retrieval remain. Section 3.3 uses more generic LLM/retrieval notation, but the implementation and Algorithm 1 retain the procedure. Appendix G's sequential strategy was already described in v1.

E1.justification: The identified coverage remains CrisisMMD classification and ScienceQA question answering. However, Appendix G newly reports a comparison on an unnamed 'smaller-scale dataset'; its description does not establish whether this is a subset of retained coverage or a different dataset/domain.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds CCOT and GraphVis while retaining the existing ScienceQA comparators. Appendix G also newly reports evaluating original CoE aggregation/selection against VaLiK's sequential approach.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Table 1 change the reported CrisisMMD text-only setting from zero-shot to few-shot prompting. Scores remain identical, and neither the shot count nor rerunning is established. Appendix F adds a separate cost example using Qwen2.5-7B for graph construction; the main implementation still specifies DeepSeek-R1-70B.

E4.justification: Appendices E–G add qualitative threshold-sensitivity observations, temperature/convergence findings, strong-single-VLM versus cascade comparisons, an aggregation-versus-sequential comparison and a construction-cost analysis. These extend the existing analyses, whose component-ablation tables, VLM-count curves and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experiments. The added appendix findings do not introduce uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds CCOT at 76.84% and GraphVis at 73.18% average accuracy; all shared entries in Tables 1–5 and the Figure 4 curves remain unchanged. Appendix F adds throughput/time estimates. Appendix G newly reports that a strong single VLM can match a cascade and that aggregation sometimes performs better than sequential processing at greater construction cost.

T1.justification: The cascade, similarity, pruning, graph-triplet and augmented-prompt equations retain their mathematical substance. Section 3.3 simplifies notation and omits an extraction mapping whose operation remains in Algorithm 1. No substantive theoretical results, assumptions or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims about autonomous construction without manual captions, storage efficiency and improved multimodal reasoning. Replacing 'Text-Free' with 'Annotation-Free' clarifies a scope already explicitly stated in v1.

C2.justification: New discussion connects clustered similarity scores to abrupt pruning changes and lower temperatures to faster ensemble consensus. It also explains accuracy–cost tradeoffs between strong models, cascades and aggregation, suggests intermediate pruning, and argues for computational scalability. Existing over-pruning and diminishing-return qualifications remain.

D1.justification: Appendices D–F expand retrieval documentation, newly specify validation-based threshold selection, and provide model-specific throughput and deployment guidance. The main thresholds, model chain, hardware specification and code-access pointer are retained; the additional detail does not establish changes to those existing settings.

R1.justification: Six references are added: GraphVis, GraphRAG, image retrieval using scene graphs, Mosaic, Fedrecon and compositional chain-of-thought prompting. Appendix G also explicitly distinguishes VaLiK's sequential design from original CoE aggregation. The broader related-work argument remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and repeated terminology change from 'Text-Free' to 'Annotation-Free', and author/affiliation ordering is edited. Section 3.3 and Appendix D receive localized rewrites; acknowledgments and Appendices E–G are added. The main narrative and section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn with different typography and proportions but unchanged plotted values, and Figure 3's labeling is simplified. Table 3 gains two rows and Table 4's caption gains abbreviation explanations. Other figures and tables are retained, with local layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The added ScienceQA baselines and threshold-selection documentation make the comparisons and implementation easier to assess, while 'Annotation-Free' states the existing scope more precisely. The gains are limited: Appendix G's additional comparisons lack detailed settings and an identified dataset, and Appendix F's cost example uses a different graph-construction model from the main experiments.
